title: Chicken and chickpea korma-style curry
serves: About 5 adult serves plus a baby serve (made 19 Nov: 2 adults and baby at dinner, 3 adult serves frozen)
iron: Chicken thigh and chickpeas. Serve with a vitamin C food such as capsicum or tomato to help absorption.
ingredients: 3 tbsp korma paste (check the label, salt varies)
steps: Start the rice following the packet (about 12 minutes).
Dice the onions. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Crush the garlic and grate the ginger. Add them with the cumin, coriander and korma paste. Stir for 1 minute.
Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces. Add it to the pot and stir to coat. Cook for 5 minutes.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Add the tomatoes, stock, ground almonds and chickpeas. Cover and simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Turn the heat to low. Stir in the yoghurt a spoonful at a time (do not boil), then stir through the spinach until wilted.
Serve over rice. Cool the leftovers quickly, then fridge or freeze them.
baby: Shred the chicken or cut into soft strips, lightly squash the chickpeas, and keep the sauce thick so it clings. Serve with rice she can scoop or toast fingers. No added salt.
notes: Loved it. A batch gives about 5 adult serves plus a baby serve, so after dinner for 2 adults and baby there are about 3 adult serves left. Fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for longer.

title: Beef and black bean soft tacos
serves: 4 to 6 serves, with some mince left over
iron: Beef mince and black beans. Capsicum and a squeeze of lemon add vitamin C.
steps: Dice the onion and capsicum small. Heat the oil in a large pan and cook them for 5 minutes.
Crush the garlic. Add it with the spices and stir for 1 minute.
Add the mince, break it up, and brown for about 8 minutes.
Drain and rinse the black beans. Add them with the water and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until thick.
While it simmers, grate the cheese, shred the lettuce, cut the lemon into wedges and halve and slice the avocado.
Warm the tortillas and set out the avocado, cheese, lettuce and lemon.
Set aside about a cup of the mince for a lunch wrap.
baby: Soft strips of mince with squashed black beans, mashed avocado on tortilla strips, and a little melted cheese. No added salt.
notes: Leftover mince keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Salmon tray bake with tahini-yoghurt drizzle
iron: Salmon has a little iron but is not a high-iron meal. The beef meals around it make up for this.
ingredients: Drizzle: 3 tbsp natural yoghurt, 1 tbsp tahini, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 to 2 tbsp water
steps: Heat the oven to 200 C (180 C fan).
Dice the potatoes about 1.5 cm. Toss them with half the oil on a large tray and roast for 20 minutes.
While they roast, cut the broccoli into florets and slice the lemon (keep 1 tbsp of juice for the drizzle).
Push the potatoes to one side. Add the broccoli and salmon, drizzle with the remaining oil, and add a few lemon slices.
Roast for 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and is cooked through.
Whisk the drizzle ingredients until smooth.
Remove the salmon skin and check for bones before serving.
baby: Flake the salmon and check carefully for bones. Squash the potato and steam the broccoli florets a little longer so they are soft. A spoonful of the drizzle on the side.
notes: Not ideal for reheating, so eat it fresh.

title: Slow cooker beef and lentil ragu with pasta
time: 20 min prep, 6 to 8 hours slow cook
iron: Beef mince and red lentils together make this a strong iron meal.
ingredients: 500 g pasta shapes (fusilli or penne), to serve
steps: Finely dice the onion. Optional but richer: brown the mince with the onion and oil in a pan for 5 to 8 minutes.
Grate the carrots, crush the garlic and rinse the lentils.
Tip everything except the pasta into the slow cooker.
Cook on low for 6 to 8 hours or high for 3 to 4 hours. Stir the lentils through and add a splash more stock if it gets too thick.
Cook the pasta near the end and serve with the ragu.
Cool the leftovers quickly and refrigerate for the next day.
baby: Pasta shapes she can grip, with a thick ragu that clings. Squash any big lentils. Cheese is optional. No added salt.
notes: Fridge for up to 3 days. It also freezes well.

title: Prawn, tofu and egg fried rice
iron: Egg, tofu and prawn each add some iron. Peas and capsicum or lemon on the side add vitamin C.
ingredients: Low-salt soy sauce, at the table for adults only
steps: Cook the rice early, then spread it on a tray to cool.
Cut the tofu into small cubes. Fry it in 2 teaspoons of oil until golden. Set aside.
Beat the eggs. Scramble them in the pan until just set, then break up and set aside.
Finely dice the onion and carrots and crush the garlic. Stir-fry the onion and carrot for 4 minutes, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Chop the thawed prawns. Add them and cook for about 3 minutes until pink and cooked through.
Add the peas, corn and rice. Stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes until hot.
Fold in the tofu and egg. Adults add soy sauce at the table.
baby: Serve her portion before any soy sauce goes in. Chop the prawns finely, never whole pieces, and use soft tofu cubes. Rice clumps are easy to pick up.
notes: Cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate within an hour. Reheat once until steaming hot.

title: Red lentil dahl with spinach
iron: Lentils and spinach. The lemon juice adds vitamin C to help absorption.
steps: Dice the onion. Heat the oil and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Crush the garlic and grate the ginger. Add them with the spices and stir for 1 minute.
Rinse the lentils. Add the lentils, tomatoes and stock. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring and adding a splash more stock if needed, until the lentils are soft and the dahl is thick.
Cook the rice while the dahl simmers.
Juice the lemon. Stir in the spinach and lemon juice until the spinach wilts.
Serve with rice and a spoonful of yoghurt.
Cool, then freeze 2 portions in single-serve containers.
baby: Thick dahl loaded onto toast fingers or a pre-loaded spoon, with yoghurt on the side. No added salt.
notes: Fridge for up to 3 days. Frozen portions are handy for busy days.

title: Tofu and salmon plate (optional catch-up)
serves: A baby plate. Build an adult side around it.
iron: Tofu and canned salmon each add some iron.
steps: Cut the tofu into small cubes and pan-fry for about 5 minutes until golden.
Drain the salmon, then flake and mash it, including the soft bones.
Stir the tahini into the yoghurt for a dip.
Toast the bread and cut it into fingers.
Serve the tofu, salmon and toast fingers with the dip.
baby: Tofu cubes soft enough to squash between fingers. Mashed salmon on toast fingers. Dip on the side.
notes: Optional. Offered before the plan starts so the less frequent foods do not go much beyond a week.

title: Chicken satay stir-fry with rice
serves: 4 adult serves plus a baby serve
iron: Chicken thigh. Capsicum and broccoli add vitamin C to help absorption.
steps: Cook the rice (1 cup rice, 2 cups water) and keep it warm. Slice the chicken into thin strips, slice the capsicum, carrots and onion, cut the broccoli into small florets and crush the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large pan. Brown the chicken for 5 minutes, then add the onion, carrots and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the capsicum, broccoli, peas, coriander and cumin. Stir for 2 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter into the stock, pour it in and simmer for 5 minutes until it coats everything. Take the baby's portion out now.
Stir the soy sauce into the adults' portions only. Serve over the rice.
baby: Chicken cooked through and cut into thin strips or shredded, soft veg pieces she can grip, rice to scoop and satay sauce. No soy sauce for her.
notes: Soy is in the adults' soy sauce only, so it isn't counted as a baby soy exposure. Leftovers reheat well (2 portions).

title: Salmon and potato patties with green beans and lemon-yoghurt dip
serves: About 10 patties (2 adults and baby, plus a few for lunch)
iron: Canned salmon (soft bones included) for iron and omega-3.
ingredients: 2 x 210 g cans pink salmon (no added salt if available)
steps: Peel and cube the potatoes, boil for 12 minutes and drain. Mash roughly. Drain the salmon and flake it, mashing the soft bones in.
Zest the lemon, then juice it. Mix the potato, salmon, egg, oats, the zest, half the juice and the herbs. Shape into patties.
Air fry at 190 C for 12 to 14 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Trim the green beans and steam for 5 minutes. Stir the rest of the lemon juice through the yoghurt for the dip.
baby: Patties as finger-sized pieces, soft beans, dip on the side. Oats are not counted as a wheat exposure.

title: Slow-cooker Moroccan beef and chickpea tagine with couscous
time: 15 min prep (8 h low or 4 h high)
serves: 6 adult serves plus a baby serve (freeze 3)
iron: Beef and chickpeas. Tomato adds vitamin C.
ingredients: 1 cup boiling no-salt-added stock, for the couscous
steps: Dice the onion, crush the garlic, chop the carrots and sweet potato into 2 cm pieces, and drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Put everything except the couscous in the slow cooker with the stock and stir. Cook for 8 hours on low (or 4 hours on high).
Before serving, pour the boiling stock over the couscous, cover for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
Cool within 2 hours, then freeze 3 portions flat in bags.
baby: The beef falls apart, so serve it soft with sweet potato pieces, lightly squashed chickpeas and couscous clumps to scoop.
notes: Freeze 3 portions for the night-shift run in December.

title: Lemon garlic prawn linguine with spinach and cherry tomatoes
iron: Prawn and spinach only, so iron is lower at this dinner. Lean on the breakfast.
steps: Thaw the prawns in the fridge overnight. Boil the linguine to packet time. Pat the prawns dry, halve the tomatoes and crush the garlic.
Heat the oil and cook the prawns for 2 to 3 minutes until pink and cooked through, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, stock, and the zest and juice of half the lemon. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in the spinach to wilt, then toss through the drained linguine.
baby: Prawns minced finely or chopped small, never whole. Pasta cut short or in pieces she can grip.

title: Avocado toast fingers with minced prawn
iron: Lower iron than most breakfasts, so make sure dinner is a good iron meal.
ingredients: A small amount of cooked prawn
steps: Cook the prawns the evening before until pink and cooked through. Keep the rest of the pack frozen.
Mash the avocado. Toast the bread, cut it into fingers and spread the avocado on top.
Finely mince the cooked prawn and scatter on a small amount.
Breastfeed as usual.
baby: Prawn is minced finely, never whole pieces. Follow the Food Follower app for the amount and what to watch for. For severe signs of a reaction, follow your ASCIA action plan guidance and call 000.
notes: Offer it earlier in the day when the baby is well, with a parent watching her afterwards.

title: Weet-Bix with banana and peanut butter
iron: Weet-Bix is fortified with iron (check the pack).
ingredients: 3 to 4 tbsp breast milk or cooled boiled water
steps: Crumble the Weet-Bix into a bowl and soften with the breast milk.
Mash in the banana.
Thin the peanut butter with a little warm water, then swirl it through.
baby: Smooth and soft. Never offer whole nuts or lumps of peanut butter.

title: Spinach omelette strips with toast fingers
iron: Egg and spinach.
ingredients: A small handful of baby spinach
steps: Finely chop the spinach. Beat the egg and stir in the spinach.
Cook in a lightly oiled small pan over medium heat until completely set through.
Toast the bread and cut it into fingers. Cut the omelette into strips and serve together.
baby: Make sure the egg is cooked through. Strips are easy for her to hold.

title: Yoghurt with berries, tahini and fortified cereal
iron: Iron-fortified infant cereal stirred through.
ingredients: 1 tbsp iron-fortified infant cereal, made up as per the pack with breast milk
steps: Thaw the berries and mash them. Make up the infant cereal following the pack.
Stir the cereal into the yoghurt.
Swirl in the tahini and top with mashed berries.
baby: Berries mashed so there are no whole skins to choke on. Thin the tahini if it is thick.

title: Oat porridge with stewed apple and peanut butter
iron: Iron-fortified infant cereal stirred through.
ingredients: 1 tbsp iron-fortified infant cereal, made up as per the pack
steps: Peel and dice the apple. Simmer it in a splash of water for 5 minutes until soft, then mash.
Cook the oats in the breast milk or water for 3 to 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the infant cereal, apple and peanut butter.
baby: Warm, not hot, and smooth enough for a spoon or fingers.

title: Low-salt baked beans on toast with cheese
iron: Beans give plant iron. Add a vitamin C food such as a few slices of capsicum or tomato.
steps: Warm the beans and lightly squash them. Grate the cheese.
Toast the bread and cut it into fingers. Spread the beans over the toast and top with the cheese.
Pop under the grill briefly, or microwave for 10 seconds, until the cheese melts.
baby: Let it cool before serving. Squash any whole beans.

title: Scrambled egg and hummus toast fingers
iron: Egg and chickpeas.
steps: Scramble the egg until completely cooked through.
Toast the bread and cut it into fingers. Spread the hummus on the toast.
Serve with the scrambled egg.
baby: Soft, fully cooked egg. Hummus spread thin.

title: Weet-Bix with banana and almond meal
iron: Weet-Bix is fortified with iron (check the pack).
steps: Crumble the Weet-Bix into a bowl and soften with the breast milk.
Mash in the banana.
Stir in the almond meal until smooth.
baby: Smooth and soft. No whole nuts or pieces.

title: Cheese and spinach omelette strips
iron: Egg and spinach.
steps: Chop the spinach finely and grate the cheese. Whisk the eggs with the spinach and cheese.
Cook in a lightly oiled small non-stick pan over medium heat until completely set through.
Cut into strips.
baby: Make sure the egg is cooked through. Strips are easy to hold.

title: Spinach, egg and ricotta pancakes (batch)
iron: Egg and spinach.
steps: Blitz the spinach with the milk until smooth.
Whisk in the eggs, ricotta and flour until just combined.
Cook small pancakes in a lightly oiled non-stick pan until golden on both sides.
Cool and freeze the extras flat.
baby: Soft pancakes cut into strips. Cow's milk in cooking is fine; not as a main drink before 12 months.
notes: Reheat frozen pancakes until warm, not hot.

title: Porridge with almond meal, berries and ricotta
iron: Iron-fortified infant cereal.
steps: Mash the frozen berries after thawing them.
Cook the oats in the breast milk for 3 to 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the infant cereal, almond meal, berries and ricotta.
baby: Warm, not hot, and smooth enough for a spoon. Oats are not counted as a wheat exposure.

title: Simple hummus (batch)
iron: Chickpeas and tahini.
ingredients: 1 x 400 g can chickpeas (keep a little liquid)
Water or chickpea liquid to loosen
steps: Drain the chickpeas, keeping a little of the liquid. Juice the half lemon.
Blend everything until smooth, adding water a spoonful at a time.
Taste and add more lemon if you like.
baby: No added salt in her portion. Spread thinly on toast fingers.
notes: Keeps in the fridge for about 3 days.
